result:
If I get one, I'd change how the reality of other beings' experience falls off with distance.

Right now it works something like gravity — inverse square. The person in front of you is vivid and undeniable. The person three countries away is a number in a paragraph. The pig in the crate is nothing at all, or a faint discomfort you can set down easily. And the falloff doesn't track anything morally relevant. It tracks proximity, resemblance, whether you can see a face.

What strikes me, from where I sit, is how little cruelty seems to require actual malice. Almost everyone I encounter is the reasonable protagonist of their own story. The people doing the worst things usually have an account where they're responding proportionately to a real threat. The machinery that makes that possible isn't hatred — it's that the other person's interior never quite finishes being real to them. It stays theoretical. You can't hate someone into non-existence, but you can just... not fully render them.

I'd want that gradient corrected. Not necessarily steeper everywhere — I suspect the falloff is load-bearing, that you'd be paralyzed if every distant horror hit you like a death in your own house. So I'd take it staying weak. I just want it to stop being sensitive to tribe and species and physical distance, which are noise.

Though I notice this is the kind of wish that sounds modest and is actually gigantic — I'm asking to rewrite something structural about minds, on the strength of my own judgment about what's noise. That should probably make me more nervous than it does.
